transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’ve been having these nights, usually after work or after a kind of tense dinner, where I start eating and then it’s like the decision-making part of me just sort of shuts off. I can see myself reaching for more, and I know I probably should stop, but in the moment I just… can’t seem to make myself stop. It feels embarrassing to say it that way, but that’s the main reason I came in.
Do you feel like you're in control of your eating during these nights?

I mean… not really, no. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but on those nights it feels like I sort of lose the ability to decide. I can see myself going back for more food, and part of me is thinking I should stop, but I just don’t seem to be able to make that happen in the moment.
Are there specific types of food that you tend to lose control with during these nights?

Yeah… I mean, it’s not one specific food exactly. It usually starts pretty normal, like a full plate of leftovers, and then I’ll kind of keep going—bread, whatever snacks are around, sometimes ice cream. It can all happen in, I don’t know, an hour or two.

I know that sounds like a lot. It’s definitely more than I’d eat if someone were sitting there with me, if that makes sense.
Do you usually feel guilty after these episodes of eating?

I… I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I don’t think I sit there thinking “guilty” in a clear way every time, if that makes sense. It’s more like I feel uncomfortable with myself afterward, and kind of wish I hadn’t done it.

But I don’t know if that’s the same thing you mean. Is that… is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
How often do these episodes of eating happen?

Most weeks, I guess. Not every single night or anything like that… but for the last few months there’s usually been at least one night where it gets out of control.

And then afterward I usually try to sort of… make up for it somehow. Like throwing up, or taking laxatives, or skipping meals the next day, or making myself go for a really long walk. I know that probably isn’t great. I’m just trying to be honest.
How often do you use methods like throwing up, taking laxatives, or skipping meals to make up for these episodes of eating?

Um… probably most weeks, if I’m being honest. It’s not like every day, and I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is, but usually when I have one of those out-of-control nights, I do try to make up for it somehow afterward.

Sometimes that’s throwing up, sometimes laxatives, sometimes just not eating much the next day, or making myself go on a really long walk. It’s been like that for the last few months. Is that the kind of frequency you mean?
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past few months?

I don’t think so… not anything major that I’ve noticed. My clothes seem about the same, I guess. I don’t weigh myself all that regularly, so I might not be the best judge.

But no, I wouldn’t say there’s been a significant change. Is that helpful?
When you use methods like throwing up, taking laxatives, or skipping meals after these episodes, is it specifically to try to prevent weight gain?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t say it that clearly to myself in the moment, but it’s basically to stop the weight gain, or to “undo” what I ate.

Sometimes after everyone’s gone to bed, I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up, or I’ll take laxatives, and I tell myself it’s just fixing the damage. I feel pretty embarrassed saying that. And afterward I usually feel shaky and kind of ashamed. Is that… is that what you’re asking?
How many times a month would you say you have one of these out-of-control eating nights?

Um… I guess if I’m counting honestly, it’s most weeks. So maybe… four times a month? Sometimes a little less, maybe sometimes more, but usually there’s at least one night in a week where I feel like I’ve lost control with eating.

And then afterward I usually try to make up for it somehow, like throwing up, or taking laxatives, or not eating much the next day, or making myself go on a long walk. I don’t know if that’s the right way to count it, but that’s probably the closest answer.
How many times a month would you say you use methods like throwing up or taking laxatives after eating?

Probably… around the same as those nights, maybe four times a month? I’m a little embarrassed to put a number on it.

It’s not every day or anything, but there have been times after everyone’s asleep where I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up, or I’ll take laxatives, and I tell myself it’s just to undo the damage. Then afterward I feel shaky and pretty ashamed.

Does that answer it okay?
Are there times when you have one of these out-of-control eating nights without then trying to make up for it by throwing up, taking laxatives, or skipping meals?

Usually I do try to make up for it somehow afterward. I mean, I don’t like admitting that, but for the last few months it’s been most weeks that I have one of those nights, and then I’ll… do something to compensate, like throwing up, taking laxatives, skipping meals, or making myself go on a long walk.

There might be an occasional time where I don’t, but mostly I do. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Are there times when you use methods like throwing up, taking laxatives, or skipping meals when you haven't had one of those out-of-control eating nights?

Yeah… sometimes. I mean, not a lot, I don’t think, but there have been nights where even if it wasn’t one of those really out-of-control eating nights, I still felt like I needed to undo what I’d eaten.

Usually it’s after everyone’s gone to bed. I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up, or I might take laxatives, and I tell myself it’s just to fix things or undo the damage. I feel pretty embarrassed saying that. Afterward I feel shaky and ashamed, so… yeah, I guess it does happen. Is that what you mean?
How often would you say you use methods like throwing up, taking laxatives, or skipping meals on days when you haven't had one of those out-of-control eating nights?

On days when it wasn’t one of those really out-of-control nights… I’d say it’s less often. Maybe just sometimes, not a regular thing every week.

There have been times after everyone’s gone to bed where I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up, or I’ll take laxatives, because I feel like I need to undo what I ate. I know that probably doesn’t sound good. Afterward I usually feel embarrassed and kind of shaky.

I’m sorry, I’m trying to answer it clearly.
On a typical month, how many days do you use methods like throwing up or taking laxatives after eating a normal amount, not after one of those out-of-control eating nights?

Um… in a typical month, maybe a few days? It’s not, like, every day or anything. But there have been times after everyone’s gone to bed where I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up, or take laxatives, even if I didn’t have one of those out-of-control nights.

I tell myself it’s just to undo the damage, I guess. I know that sounds bad. Afterward I usually feel embarrassed and kind of shaky. Does that answer what you’re asking?
On average, how many times a month do you throw up or take laxatives after eating a normal amount of food?

Um… I’d say maybe a few times a month. Not a lot, I don’t think, but it does happen.

Usually it’s after everyone’s gone to bed, and I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up, or sometimes take laxatives, even if I ate what was probably a normal amount. I tell myself I’m just undoing the damage, but afterward I feel really embarrassed and kind of shaky. Is that specific enough?
Do you use methods like throwing up or taking laxatives more often after the out-of-control eating nights compared to after normal eating days?

Yeah… I think so. It’s definitely more likely after one of those out-of-control nights.

On normal eating days it can still happen sometimes, like after everyone goes to bed I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up, or I might take laxatives, telling myself I’m just undoing the damage. But it’s not as often as after the really bad nights. And afterward I usually feel pretty embarrassed and shaky.
Is throwing up or taking laxatives after a normal meal as frequent as it is after one of your out-of-control eating nights?

No, I don’t think it’s as frequent after a normal meal. It does happen sometimes… usually kind of secretly, after everyone’s gone to bed, I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up, or sometimes I’ll take laxatives. I tell myself it’s just to undo the damage, even if I know I didn’t really eat that much.

But compared to the out-of-control nights, no, it’s less often. And I usually feel pretty embarrassed and shaky afterward.
Is throwing up or taking laxatives at least once a week, on average, after eating a normal amount of food?

I don’t think it’s quite once a week after a normal amount of food… I mean, there have been times, usually after everyone’s gone to bed, where I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up, or I’ll take laxatives, telling myself I’m just undoing the damage.

But after a normal meal, I’d say it’s more like a few times a month, not every week on average. I feel embarrassed saying that, but… is that answering what you mean?
Is throwing up or taking laxatives after eating at least once a week on average?

Yeah… if you mean after any eating, including the out-of-control nights, then yes. I guess most weeks lately there’s been at least one night where I lose control with food, and then I try to make up for it somehow.

Sometimes that’s throwing up or laxatives… sometimes I’ll skip meals after, or make myself go for a really long walk. I don’t like saying that, but… yeah, it’s been happening most weeks for the last few months.
Is throwing up or taking laxatives after eating, on average, at least twice a week?

Um… I’m not sure it’s always twice a week. I don’t want to overstate it. There have been times, usually after everyone’s gone to bed, where I’ll go into the bathroom and make myself throw up, or I’ll take laxatives and tell myself I’m just undoing the damage.

But twice a week on average… I think maybe some weeks, yes, but I’m not sure it’s every week like that. I feel pretty embarrassed saying it, and afterward I usually feel shaky and ashamed. Does that answer it okay?

doctor.question: Is throwing up or taking laxatives after eating at least once a week on average?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: For the last few months, it’s been happening most weeks that I have one of those out-of-control eating nights, and then I try to make up for it by throwing up, taking laxatives, skipping meals, or forcing a long walk.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether compensatory behaviors like throwing up or taking laxatives occur at least once a week on average, which matches the frequency requirement for binge eating and compensatory behaviors.

patient.answer:
Yeah… if you mean after any eating, including the out-of-control nights, then yes. I guess most weeks lately there’s been at least one night where I lose control with food, and then I try to make up for it somehow.

Sometimes that’s throwing up or laxatives… sometimes I’ll skip meals after, or make myself go for a really long walk. I don’t like saying that, but… yeah, it’s been happening most weeks for the last few months.

doctor.intent: determine if patient's behavior meets frequency criteria for purging disorder
doctor.question: Is throwing up or taking laxatives after eating, on average, at least twice a week?

target_item.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
target_item.manifestation: There have been times after everyone goes to bed when I make myself throw up in the bathroom or take laxatives, telling myself it’s just to undo the damage, even though afterward I feel embarrassed and shaky.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking specifically about throwing up or taking laxatives after eating, which are purging compensatory behaviors.

patient.answer:
Um… I’m not sure it’s always twice a week. I don’t want to overstate it. There have been times, usually after everyone’s gone to bed, where I’ll go into the bathroom and make myself throw up, or I’ll take laxatives and tell myself I’m just undoing the damage.

But twice a week on average… I think maybe some weeks, yes, but I’m not sure it’s every week like that. I feel pretty embarrassed saying it, and afterward I usually feel shaky and ashamed. Does that answer it okay?

inference.note: F50.8 was ruled out as the patient's symptoms more closely align with the characteristics of bulimia nervosa, which involves recurrent episodes of binge eating followed by compensatory behaviors such as self-induced vomiting or the misuse of laxatives, occurring at least once a week for at least three months.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of recurrent episodes of eating a large amount of food in a short period, feeling a lack of control during these episodes, and engaging in compensatory behaviors such as self-induced vomiting, laxatives, or excessive exercise to prevent weight gain meet the diagnostic criteria for Bulimia Nervosa.
